synthesis: Admin 'Login as Scout user' intermittently fails with NO error during consecutive impersonations. Demo 2026-09-16 showed force-login working, then stopping for 3 different Scout users consecutively. Ticket filed day after PR #410 merge (2026-09-15), which fixed duplicate-GET token revocation but introduced a session-tracking mechanism that accumulates token IDs across DIFFERENT drivers without scoping. Root cause: Session::push() appends each driver's token ID to a single session array; when revokeTracked() fires (on impersonation exit/entry), it deletes ALL accumulated tokens including still-open tabs. Silent failure occurs because revocation happens AFTER admin closes force-login modal/flow, so 401s hit when admin isn't watching.

scope.summary: Fix cross-driver token revocation in ScoutForceTokens session tracking. Scope session array to per-driver tracking OR clear array between consecutive force-logins. Add client-side validation for missing/malformed forceAuth payload. Preserve PR #410 fixes (duplicate GET tolerance, 3-token retention, service worker exclusion).

proposed_changes.change: Scope session tracking to driver ID: change SESSION_KEY from flat array to keyed structure ['driver_123' => [token_ids]]. mintFor() pushes to driver-specific sub-array; revokeTracked() accepts optional User param to revoke single driver, or revokes ALL if no param. OR: clear entire session array on each mintFor() call (simpler but loses multi-tab support for SAME driver).
proposed_changes.reason: Current Session::push appends all drivers' token IDs to one array; revokeTracked() deletes ALL, causing cross-driver revocation. Driver-scoped tracking prevents Driver A's token being revoked when admin force-logins Driver B.

proposed_changes.change: Add validation: abort_if(empty($token), 500, 'Failed to mint force token'); log warning if driver has stale tokens (indicates session state issue); ensure activity log fires even on edge-case failures.
proposed_changes.reason: Ticket reports NO error message; if mintFor() returns empty string or null (unlikely but defensive), controller would embed malformed payload and PWA would boot broken.

proposed_changes.change: Add validation before forceAuthenticate(): if window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ exists but .token/.user/.kit are missing/null/empty, navigate to /scout/login with explicit sessionStorage reason 'Force-login payload invalid' instead of silently booting broken state.
proposed_changes.reason: If controller returns 200 with malformed payload, PWA boots but auth fails silently; matches ticket's 'NO error message' symptom.

proposed_changes.change: OPTIONAL: Move revokeTracked() call to AFTER session()->invalidate() OR add explicit Session::forget(SESSION_KEY) before invalidate() to ensure stale array doesn't persist in memory if admin re-impersonates in same browser. (Low priority if primary fix is driver-scoped tracking.)
proposed_changes.reason: Line 32 revokeTracked() reads session array, line 35 invalidates session; if admin re-impersonates without full browser refresh, old array might persist. Defensive fix but primary issue is accumulation, not ordering.

proposed_changes.change: Add test: test_consecutive_force_logins_of_different_drivers_within_one_admin_session - force-login 3 different drivers with admin_impersonator session, verify all 3 tokens remain valid and no cross-driver revocation occurs. Covers the exact failure scenario from ticket.
proposed_changes.reason: Existing tests only cover duplicate GET of SAME driver or single-driver scenarios; MISSING test for consecutive DIFFERENT drivers - the reported bug.
proposed_changes.ref: lines 87-104 test same driver twice; need test for Driver A, B, C

questions.q: Was Premier Adjusters demo environment running PR #410 deploy (merged 2026-09-15) at time of incident (2026-09-16)?
Did admin re-impersonate (new /auth/impersonate) between working force-login and 3 failures, or all within one continuous impersonation session?
Were the 3 Scout users in same org or different orgs? (Different orgs require re-impersonation)
Did admin keep prior force-login tabs open while trying subsequent users, or close each before opening next?
What exactly does 'stopped loading' mean - 403/404 response OR 200 with view that failed to boot PWA?
Were any of the 3 target Scout users actively logged in on own devices when admin tried to force-login?
Product decision: Should force-login kick out active driver's normal session, or coexist? Current code allows both.
Does Session::push() create cumulative array across consecutive force-logins of different drivers?
questions.answer: YES - line 49 Session::push(SESSION_KEY, token_id) appends to single array without driver scoping; consecutive Driver A→B→C accumulates [A_token, B_token, C_token]; revokeTracked() deletes ALL

questions.q: When does revokeTracked() fire - only on impersonation entry/exit or elsewhere?
questions.answer: Three call sites only: ImpersonateController@impersonate line 32 (new impersonation), @leave line 83, @exitAdminMode line 94; NOT called during normal force-login flow

questions.answer: NO - ClarityScoutAuthController line 64 deletes where('name', 'clarity-scout-token') which does NOT match 'clarity-scout-force-token'; intentionally different names for safe coexistence

grounding.code_flow: Admin clicks 'Login to Scout' in Filament Scout Users Resource → GET /scout/force-login/{kit} (new tab) → ClarityScoutForceLoginController checks admin_impersonator session (line 16) → ScoutForceTokens::mintFor(driver) creates token + Session::push(SESSION_KEY, token_id) APPENDS to flat array (line 49) → prune(driver) keeps 3 most recent per driver (line 51) → blade renders clarity-scout view with window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ → PWA main.js reads payload (NO validation), calls auth.forceAuthenticate() → store sets token, connects Echo → app boots. CROSS-DRIVER ACCUMULATION: Admin force-logins Driver A, B, C consecutively → session array accumulates [A_token, B_token, C_token] → Admin exits impersonation or starts new impersonation → ImpersonateController calls revokeTracked() → Session::pull(SESSION_KEY) retrieves ALL IDs → PersonalAccessToken::query()->whereIn('id', ALL_IDS)->delete() → ALL THREE tokens deleted → All three tabs 401 on next poll. SILENT FAILURE: If admin already closed force-login modal, 401s hit when admin not watching; Login.vue would show reason but admin never sees it.

escalate.reason: High confidence on root cause (Session::push accumulation without driver scoping) but auth/session is blast-radius sensitive - a bug here locks users out or leaks tokens. Timeline (ticket day after PR #410 merge) and demo context (Premier Adjusters) suggest production impact. AC5 requires product decision (single-login enforcement). Fix is straightforward (driver-scoped session map) but needs human review to choose between: (1) driver-scoped map ['driver_123'=>[ids]], (2) clear session array on each mint (loses multi-tab for SAME driver), (3) accept accumulation and only revoke on explicit leave (changes revocation timing). Recommend pairing with PR #410 author (Dalton per commit 83fb68d24) to ensure no regression and alignment on session lifecycle. Also need confirmation from user/PM on demo state (was PR #410 deployed? exact failure sequence?).
